messages:
alex.chang: urgent — acme-corp reporting TLS timeouts to their Private inference endpoint (10.2.4.5:443) behind a NAT gateway. curl just hangs, no TLS handshake. customer calls our hosted API from inside their VPC. any quick ideas?

support-bot: ticket #ACME-492 created and linked to this thread.

maria.g: thanks alex. can you paste the minimal repro (curl + tcpdump) and confirm whether they're using custom NACLs or just default? also which AZ/region?

alex.chang: quick repro they gave: `curl -v --connect-timeout 10 https://10.2.4.5:443` -> output ends with `* Connection timed out after 10000 milliseconds`
They ran `tcpdump -nn -i eth0 host 10.2.4.5 and port 443` on the NAT instance and see repeated SYN from 10.2.4.100:53124 -> 10.2.4.5:443 but no SYN-ACK back. Sample line: `10.2.4.100.53124 > 10.2.4.5.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 29200, length 0`
Customer says they have a locked-down NACL and a custom SG.

samir.netops: probable NACL/SG return-path issue. Quick checklist: are their NACLs stateful? (NACLs are stateless) If NACL denies ephemeral port ranges on the return direction the server's SYN-ACK won't get through. Ask them to verify both NACL inbound/outbound rules.

samir.netops: run these checks on their side:
```
# check SG outbound allows 443
aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids sg-xxxx --query 'SecurityGroups[].IpPermissionsEgress'
# check NACL rules
aws ec2 describe-network-acls --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-xxxxx
```
Also run `sudo tcpdump -nn -i ethX 'tcp and host 10.2.4.100 and port 443'` on the inference ENI to see if SYNs arrive.

maria.g: to make it concrete — common gotcha: NACL has an explicit DENY for ephemeral ports (1024-65535) outbound. Because NACLs are evaluated for both directions, a client connecting from ephemeral src port 53124 to destination 443 requires the NACL to allow ephemeral return traffic. If they only allowed 443 inbound and denied ephemeral outbound, return SYN-ACK gets dropped.

alex.chang: they ran `aws ec2 describe-network-acls` and pasted rules. I see rule 100 deny 1024-65535 for egress.

samir.netops: yep that's it. Two remediation options:
1) Modify the NACL to allow ephemeral ports (TCP 1024-65535) for the relevant subnet(s) — both inbound and outbound entries as needed.
2) Use a stateful construct (SG/NAT) where security groups handle return traffic so you don't need bi-directional NACL rules.

samir.netops: example NACL allow entries (replace rule numbers accordingly):
```
# allow return ephemeral
RuleNumber: 110, Protocol: TCP (6), PortRange: 1024-65535, Egress: true, Action: ALLOW, CidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
RuleNumber: 110, Protocol: TCP (6), PortRange: 1024-65535, Egress: false, Action: ALLOW, CidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0
```

maria.g: also confirm there's no intermediate firewall in the customer's on-prem or corporate egress allowlist blocking ephemeral ports. sometimes customers allow only 443/80 and do TLS inspection which breaks direct 443-to-private-IP calls.

alex.chang: asked customer to add ephemeral allow rules and to temporarily open SG egress to 0.0.0.0/0 for testing. they reported back after changes.

support-bot: update: #ACME-492 status -> investigating (netops engaged).

alex.chang: after adding NACL allow for 1024-65535 (both directions) the tcpdump on the NAT shows SYN -> SYN-ACK and curl now completes the TLS handshake. customer confirms inference calls succeed and latency is normal. :tada:

maria.g: great — recommend they keep minimal allowed CIDRs rather than 0.0.0.0/0 if possible (limit to the subnets/VPC ranges). Also added runbook note: "When troubleshooting private inference connectivity, verify NACLs allow ephemeral port ranges for return traffic."

samir.netops: marking root cause = NACL egress deny of ephemeral ports. closing once customer confirms for 24h.

alex.chang: customer will monitor, closing on our side after 24h. thanks team :thumbsup:
